items.title: The Value of Thinking: Learning When to Reason in Hybrid Decision Models
items.snippet: Existing adaptive-reasoning methods shorten the explicit reasoning a model writes, or skip it by switching modes; either way the answer is still written out token by token. Rather than deciding how much to think, we explore a different paradigm, zero-or-T thinking: a single model either answers from the implicit thinking inside one forward pass, generating no token, or performs full autoregressive reasoning at a cost of T tokens when that is worth paying. We realise it in a hybrid decision model (HDM), where one frozen backbone serves both modes and a lightweight self-routing block chooses between them. The block estimates the value of thinking, the utility the slow mode is expected to add o
items.title_ar: Zero-or-T Thinking: تعلم متى يفكر النموذج
items.summary_ar: تقترح الورقة paradigm جديد يسمى zero-or-T thinking، حيث يجيب النموذج إما من التفكير الضمني داخل forward pass واحد دون توليد tokens، أو يقوم بـ reasoning كامل بتكلفة T tokens عند الحاجة. تُنفذ الفكرة عبر hybrid decision model يشترك فيه backbone مجمد مع block توجيه ذاتي خفيف يقدّر قيمة التفكير. الهدف هو تقليل تكلفة inference مع الحفاظ على جودة الإجابات.
items.why_ar: يهم هذا المهندس لأنه يمس التحكم في تكلفة inference وlatency عند بناء agents وتطبيقات LLM في الإنتاج.
items.title_en: Zero-or-T Thinking: Learning When to Reason
items.summary_en: The paper proposes zero-or-T thinking, where a single model either answers with implicit reasoning in one forward pass or performs full autoregressive reasoning at T tokens. It realizes this in a hybrid decision model with a frozen backbone and a lightweight self-routing block that estimates the value of thinking. The goal is to cut inference cost while preserving answer quality.
items.why_en: It directly affects how you control inference cost and latency when building LLM agents for production.

items.title: Who Remembers What? Multi-Granularity Memory Extraction for Multi-User, Multi-Agent Interaction
items.snippet: Self-evolving agents improve their own skills, memory, and harness code from experience without retraining the base LLM, and group-evolving agents go further by sharing these lessons across agents. Yet most such systems overlook that sharing across users and heterogeneous agents requires deciding who can benefit from each lesson and what information must remain private. We present MixUA, a memory system that distills independent user-agent trajectories into lessons and assigns each lesson to a user-agent pair, user, agent, or global scope according to whom it benefits and what it may disclose. For evaluation, we introduce CrossLearnBench, a mixed-user-agent benchmark that pairs established a
items.title_ar: ذاكرة MixUA للوكلاء المتعددين تحدد من يستفيد من كل lesson
items.summary_ar: يقدم البحث MixUA، وهو memory system يحوّل trajectories المستقلة لكل user-agent pair إلى lessons، ثم يسند كل lesson إلى نطاق user-agent pair أو user أو agent أو global حسب من يستفيد منه وما يمكن كشفه. كما يقدم CrossLearnBench كـ benchmark مختلط لتقييم هذا النوع من التعلم المشترك بين المستخدمين والوكلاء.
items.why_ar: يهمك لأن أنظمة agents في البنك تخدم مستخدمين متعددين وتحتاج فصل المعلومات الخاصة عن الدروس المشتركة.
items.title_en: MixUA: Scoped Memory Sharing Across Users and Agents
items.summary_en: The paper proposes MixUA, a memory system that distills independent user-agent trajectories into lessons and scopes each lesson to a user-agent pair, a user, an agent, or globally. Scope is decided by who benefits and what information may be disclosed. It also introduces CrossLearnBench, a mixed-user-agent benchmark for evaluation.
items.why_en: It addresses privacy-aware memory sharing across users in multi-agent systems, a design problem you will face when building agents for bank customers and staff.

items.title: Back to Pixels: Lifting Latent Video Diffusion into Pixel Space
items.snippet: Frontier video generation models work in a VAE latent space that compresses video in both space and time. This compression made training tractable, but now limits high-resolution, controllable, and interactive generation -- doubling resolution quadruples token count, conditions apply to groups of frames rather than individual ones, and each response must wait for the rest of its multi-frame block. We present PixVid, a simple yet effective method that lifts a pretrained latent video model to directly generate every frame in pixel space. PixVid keeps the diffusion transformer and replaces the VAE decoder with a convolutional head that renders its outputs into pixels. We find that predicting cl
items.title_ar: PixVid: توليد الفيديو مباشرة في pixel space بدلاً من VAE
items.summary_ar: تقترح ورقة PixVid رفع موديل latent video diffusion مدرب مسبقاً ليولّد كل إطار مباشرة في pixel space. تحافظ الطريقة على diffusion transformer وتستبدل VAE decoder برأس convolutional يحوّل المخرجات إلى pixels.
items.why_ar: يهم المهندس بشكل محدود لأنه بحث في توليد الفيديو، لكنه يوضح قيود ضغط VAE latent في نماذج التوليد الحديثة.
items.title_en: PixVid: Lifting Latent Video Diffusion into Pixel Space
items.summary_en: The PixVid paper proposes lifting a pretrained latent video model to generate every frame directly in pixel space. It keeps the diffusion transformer and replaces the VAE decoder with a convolutional head that renders outputs into pixels.
items.why_en: It is a generative video research paper that highlights limits of VAE latent compression for high-resolution and interactive generation.

items.title: Unbundling Multimodal Vision Encoding
items.snippet: How multimodal language models should encode visual input remains up for debate. Most models use a pretrained vision encoder, while some recent recipes train the encoder from scratch with the language model or remove it entirely. Vision encoders bundle together three design choices: a visual prior from upstream pretraining, dedicated vision capacity, and pre-fusion placement of that capacity (i.e., before the multimodal backbone). Because published models also differ in data, architecture, and compute, comparing them cannot isolate the effect of each choice. We disentangle these choices via a controlled framework where we pretrain all models from scratch on common data and compare them on vi
items.title_ar: Unbundling Multimodal Vision Encoding: فك ارتباط مكونات الرؤية
items.summary_ar: تدرس الورقة كيفية ترميز الصور في multimodal language models، وتفصل بين ثلاثة عناصر تتداخل عادة في vision encoders: visual prior من pretraining، والسعة المخصصة للرؤية، وموضع هذه السعة قبل الـ fusion. تدرب الورقة جميع النماذج من الصفر على بيانات مشتركة لعزل تأثير كل عنصر. النتيجة تقدم مقارنة أكثر دقة مما توفره النماذج المنشورة التي تختلف في البيانات والمعمارية والحوسبة.
items.why_ar: تفيد هذه الورقة المهندس في اختيار معمارية multimodal عند بناء POCs تعتمد على الصور والمستندات.
items.title_en: Unbundling Multimodal Vision Encoding
items.summary_en: The paper disentangles three bundled design choices in vision encoders: upstream visual priors, dedicated vision capacity, and pre-fusion placement. It pretrains all models from scratch on common data to isolate the effect of each choice. The comparison aims to clarify which design decisions actually matter for multimodal models.
items.why_en: It helps you choose a multimodal architecture when building document or image understanding POCs.

items.title: Experience-Handoff Reinforcement Learning for Recursive Self-Improvement
items.snippet: It is common to train Large Language Models (LLMs) for agentic tasks with Reinforcement Learning (RL) from scalar rewards. However, this throws away the fine-grained information about the environment that the agent experienced during the trial (e.g., error logs). To utilize this rich information, recent works wrap the agent in a harness that refines its own inputs through reflection or compaction and hands past experience to future rollouts, but the construction of the handed-off artifacts (e.g., a playbook) is itself not learned. We want the best of both worlds: gradient updates from a scalar reward, while also utilizing environment information to hand off experience. As a concrete testbed,
items.title_ar: Experience-Handoff RL: تعلم تسليم الخبرة للـ agents
items.summary_ar: تقترح الورقة طريقة تدريب LLM للمهام agentic باستخدام reinforcement learning من مكافأة scalar، مع الاستفادة من معلومات البيئة مثل error logs. تتعلم الطريقة أيضاً كيفية بناء الـ artifacts التي تُسلَّم للتجارب المستقبلية، مثل playbook، بدلاً من تركها ثابتة. تُختبر الفكرة على مهمة محددة لدعم فكرة recursive self-improvement.
items.why_ar: يهم المهندس لأنه يمس تدريب agents وكيفية تحسينها من تجارب التنفيذ الفعلية.
items.title_en: Experience-Handoff RL for Recursive Self-Improvement
items.summary_en: The paper trains LLM agents with reinforcement learning from scalar rewards while also using rich environment feedback such as error logs. It learns how to construct the experience artifacts, like a playbook, handed to future rollouts instead of keeping them fixed. The approach is tested on a concrete agentic testbed.
items.why_en: It is relevant if you build or evaluate agents that must improve from their own execution traces.

items.title: The Narrative Gap: Can LLMs Help Us Navigate Diverse Narratives Across Languages?
items.snippet: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly mediate how people seek and consume information, including accounts that differ across languages and regions, especially on contested topics. Supporting diverse information seeking requires models to help users navigate competing narratives across languages and information streams. items.title_ar: The Narrative Gap: مساعدة LLMs على تنوع الروايات عبر اللغات
items.summary_ar: تعرّف الورقة ست قدرات لازمة لبحث المعلومات المتنوع متعدد اللغات، تشمل إدراج الروايات واستبعادها وتحديد الروايات المفقودة. تتناول أيضاً عرض الروايات المتنوعة والحفاظ على تغطيتها عند الاستعلامات التأكيدية وتحقيق تكافؤ المعلومات بين اللغات. الهدف هو قياس قدرة LLMs على مساعدة المستخدمين في التنقل بين الروايات المتنافسة حول الموضوعات الخلافية.
items.why_ar: يهم المهندس بشكل هامشي عند بناء أنظمة بحث متعددة اللغات، لكنه بعيد عن أولويات عمله المصرفي.
items.title_en: The Narrative Gap: Can LLMs Navigate Diverse Narratives Across Languages?
items.summary_en: The paper defines six capabilities for diverse multilingual information seeking, covering narrative inclusion, exclusion, and identification of missing narratives. It also covers presenting diverse narratives, preserving coverage under confirmatory queries, and maintaining information parity across languages. The goal is to evaluate how well LLMs help users navigate competing narratives on contested topics.
items.why_en: It is useful if you build multilingual search or retrieval systems, but it is not a core banking concern.
